outcome: Nutrient composition of human milk (including various fatty acids, calcium, phosphorus, iodine, and fucosyl-sialyl-lacto-N-tetraose 2)
finding: While unadjusted analyses showed some differences in the nutrient composition of human milk between mothers who delivered by cesarean section and those who delivered vaginally, these differences were not statistically significant after adjusting for confounding factors.
mod_finding: Milk from mothers who had C-sections had higher ratios of arachidonic acid/docosahexaenoic acid (ARA/DHA) and n-6/n-3, as well as higher polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA)% in unadjusted analyses.
